findings.statement: Scope: one bounded replay (run:5ce89f521e5e, 50,000 dataset events, 3 of 3 jobs completed, clink exit status 0, not cancelled; fan-in threshold 5 distinct senders per 3,600,000 ms event-time window; onward links require a gap of at most 1,800,000 ms). The graph holds 50,000 transfers, 12,072 accounts, 12,321 devices, 691 onward links and 6 fan-in alerts. Everything below holds only for this dataset as this run processed it.

Alert fan_in:A-10859:1794924000000: A-10859 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders between 1794924000000 and 1794927600000, totalling 204,000 minor units (T011431, T011465, T011494, T011536, T011572, T011610).

Alert fan_in:A-20636:1795190400000: A-20636 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders between 1795190400000 and 1795194000000, totalling 36,000 (T033316, T033368, T033403, T033439, T033474, T033495).

Alert fan_in:A-85921:1794855600000: A-85921 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders between 1794855600000 and 1794859200000, totalling 15,000 (T005750, T005789, T005830, T005868, T005934, T005978).

A-10859 onward routes: at most 3 onward links. All six contributing transfers are linked onward to A-10859's debits T011583 (150,000) and/or T011670 (95,000), both paid to A-78340. A-78340 then sent T011600 (120,000) to A-75793, which sent T011628 (117,500) to A-92332, and T011695 (118,000) to A-85287. The money comes to rest at two accounts, A-92332 and A-85287. Route accounts: A-10859, A-78340, A-75793, A-92332, A-85287.

A-20636 onward route: at most 1 onward link. Five of the six contributing transfers are linked to T033506 (30,000), which A-20636 paid to A-36729, and it was not passed on. T033316 (the earliest contribution, at 1795190580000) has no onward link. The money comes to rest at A-36729.

A-28137 onward route: no onward links at all. None of its seven contributing transfers was passed on, so it has no chain and no resting account beyond A-28137. A-28137's only recorded outgoing transfer, T018852 (21,000 to A-87539 at 1795013700000), is not an onward link from any contribution and was not itself passed on.

A-37573 onward routes: at most 4 onward links, along two parallel sequences through the same accounts. T003057, T003091, T003124 and T003154 link to T003168, which runs A-37573 -> A-38045 -> A-93288 -> A-63022 -> A-54215 (T003168, T003182, T003201, T003222). T003248, T003287 and T003319 link to T003391, which follows the same account sequence (T003391, T003416, T003433, T003454). Both end at A-54215 (184,000 + 166,000). Every contributing transfer is passed on.

A-83577 onward route: at most 5 onward links, the longest of the six alerts. All eight contributing transfers link to T022572 (172,000), and the money then runs A-83577 -> A-56768 -> A-83094 -> A-43725 -> A-14799 -> A-39382 (T022572, T022592, T022609, T022629, T022649). It comes to rest at A-39382 (161,500).

A-85921 onward route: at most 1 onward link. T005750, T005789, T005830 and T005868 link to T005888 (9,500), which A-85921 paid to A-10758, and it was not passed on. T005934 and T005978 have no onward link. The money comes to rest at A-10758.

Shared devices on routes (question 3): on A-10859's route, device D-79802 sent transfers from A-10859 and A-78340. On A-37573's route, device D-45880 sent transfers from A-37573, A-38045, A-93288 and A-63022, and it sent all eight onward transfers. On A-83577's route, device D-40018 sent transfers from A-83094 (T022609) and A-14799 (T022649). The same device also sent T038409 from A-34114, an account that is not on the route. The routes of A-20636, A-28137 and A-85921 have no device used by two or more route accounts.

What distinguishes the alerts (question 4): as indicators they look alike (6 to 8 distinct senders, one transfer per sender, one hour). The recorded relationships separate them into three groups. (a) A-28137 has no onward links. (b) A-20636 and A-85921 each have a single 1-link hop to one resting account, some contributions not passed on, and no shared device on the route. (c) A-10859, A-37573 and A-83577 have multi-hop chains (3, 4 and 5 links) that pass on every contribution, and each route has a device shared by route accounts. Within (c), A-37573 is the strongest: one device (D-40018) covers the alerted account and all three intermediaries. A-10859 shares a device between the alerted account and its first hop, and it splits to two resting accounts. In A-83577, two non-adjacent intermediaries share a device. None of the resting accounts (A-92332, A-85287, A-36729, A-54215, A-39382, A-10758) has a fan-in alert of its own.

hypotheses.statement: On the A-37573 route, one device sent from four accounts and the money passed through the same four-hop sequence twice. This pattern fits a single party controlling the alerted account and its intermediaries, i.e. layering towards A-54215. Device sharing does not establish ownership or identity.
The A-10859 and A-83577 routes, with multi-hop pass-through and partial device sharing, may be rapid pass-through (mule-style) activity. This is an interpretation only.

A-28137 received many small payments and passed none of them on within the onward window. That fits ordinary collection activity (for example a merchant or a shared expense), so its alert may be of lower priority. A-20636 and A-85921, which have one hop and no device overlap, are intermediate cases.

unresolved.question: What happens to the money after the resting accounts (A-92332, A-85287, A-36729, A-54215, A-39382, A-10758)? Within this dataset none of their resting transfers was passed on. Any later movement outside the bounded dataset cannot be observed.

Do the shared devices (D-79802, D-45880, D-40018) reflect common control, a shared or public device, or device-ID collisions? Is A-34114, which also used D-40018, related to the A-83577 route? The data records only device usage.
A-10859's two onward debits (245,000 in total) exceed its alerted inflow (204,000). Does that reflect other credits or an earlier balance? The source of the difference was not established here.
What is the relationship between the contributing senders and the alerted accounts? Is the fan-in coordinated or coincidental? Nothing recorded answers this.
